name: Kim St-Cyr
title: Program Officer, Climate Engagement Canada @ Shareholder Association of Research and Education (SHARE)
bio:
Kim St-Cyr is a multidisciplinary sustainability professional with a Master of Science in Sustainability Management and an Honors Bachelor of Science in Environmental Science, both from the University of Toronto. She currently serves as a Program Officer for Climate Engagement Canada (CEC) at the Shareholder Association of Research and Education (SHARE), where she coordinates and supports collaborative investor engagements that drive corporate climate action and advance Canada's net-zero transition. CEC is an investor-led engagement initiative with 61 institutional investors representing approximately ~$14.5 trillion in AUM and focuses on driving Canada's business transition to net zero.
Prior to working at SHARE, Kim completed a graduate internship at the Canadian Medical Association (CMA) Impact, where she gained hands-on experience with the development of proxy voting guidelines, harnessing investor engagement mechanisms, and participating in investor coalitions focused on advancing ESG issues. Her expertise in shareholder engagement extends beyond professional practice. Her master's thesis examined the impact of shareholder proposals on greenhouse gas (GHG) disclosure and target-setting, and their relationship with firm-level ESG and emissions performance.
Kim continues to expand her knowledge of sustainability and seeks to build connections that foster innovative and purpose-driven approaches to addressing sustainability challenges.

name: Sanjida Moury
title: Senior Engineer @ Toronto Transit Commission
bio: Dr. Sanjida Moury is an electrical engineer specializing in renewable energy and transportation electrification, currently serving as a Senior Engineer in the Renewable Energy Program within the Innovation and Sustainability Group at the Toronto Transit Commission (TTC), where she advances eBus infrastructure, operations, and renewable integration. Holding a Ph.D. from York University, she previously worked as an Assistant Professor at Lakehead University, following industry experience as a Board Designer at Advanced Micro Devices (AMD). Her work focuses on system design and optimization for green applications, improving efficiency, reliability, and cost-effectiveness in electrified transportation and renewable power systems, with publications in leading journals and conferences. An active contributor to IEEE technical and conference committees and a Board Director for Women in Renewable Energy (WiRE), Dr. Moury is committed to building a sustainable future and empowering women in STEM.

name: Alicia Battaglia
title: Postdoctoral Research Fellow, Bazylak Group @ University of Toronto
bio:
Alicia Battaglia is a postdoctoral fellow at the University of Toronto working with Prof. Aimy Bazylak on developing novel ionomers and catalysts for CO2 electrolysis. She completed her Ph.D. in polymer and materials chemistry at the University of Toronto in 2024 under the supervision of Prof. Dwight S. Seferos, where her research focused on the design of polymer binders for organic electrodes. Prior to this, Alicia earned her B.Sc. (Honours Specialization in Chemistry) from Western University in 2019, where she conducted undergraduate research with Profs. Joe Gilroy and John Corrigan on semiconducting materials for resistive memory applications.
Her research interests include polymer and materials, energy storage, and sustainable electrochemical systems. Alicia has authored 14 publications, including six as first-author, and was awarded the Chair's Doctoral Medal for her Ph.D. thesis. She is passionate about equity, diversity, inclusion and sustainability, having held leadership roles on student organizations such as Working Towards Inclusivity in Chemistry Toronto (WICTO) and the Green Chemistry Initiative (GCI). She is also deeply committed to mentorship, outreach, and teaching, contributing to programs such as Girls in SySTEM and Science Rendezvous.

name: Eman Abdelsabour
title: Senior Architect, Sustainability Lead @ BDP Quadrangle
bio:
Eman A. Sabour is an architect and sustainability strategist specializing in embodied carbon, climate-responsive design, and the integration of ESG principles into real project delivery. Her work spans architecture, urban design, and systems thinking, with a focus on creating practical tools, metrics, and workflows that help design teams deliver efficient, low-carbon, and high-performance projects. Eman has developed multi-dimensional frameworks and digital integration tools that embed carbon literacy, accessibility, wellness, and resilience directly into everyday design practice.
Throughout her career, she has championed approaches that bring performance, health, and equity together, strengthening how buildings support both people and the planet. Her interdisciplinary mindset allows her to translate technical complexity into clear strategies that designers, clients, and city partners can use to meet climate and sustainability goals with confidence.
Based in Toronto, Eman is committed to shaping a built environment where environmental responsibility and social impact are inseparable, practical, and achievable project by project, team by team.

name: Sarah Syed
title: Climate Justice Advocate @ United Nations Habitat Youth Advisory Board
bio: Sarah Syed is a climate justice advocate and a member of the United Nations Habitat Youth Advisory Board. With a passion for climate education, policy advocacy, and intergenerational collaboration, Sarah has worked extensively with non-profits to develop environmental programs. Notably, she organized the Top 25 Under 25 Environmentalists in Canada program, which supports young leaders with funding and mentorship, and designed the first community engagement project at the Bay Area Climate Change Council (Burlington/Hamilton). Sarah has also organized one of the largest youth environmental hackathons globally with over 1000 participants and $42,000 in prizes awarded to youth to scale projects. An avid public speaker, Sarah has presented at numerous conferences including the United Nations, World Environmental Education Congress, AWE USA, and received several accolades, including being named the youngest Developer 30 Under 30, and receiving 2x recognition from the Lieutenant Governor for her conservation efforts and dedication to engaging youth in climate policy.
